source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Attached are the files and the brief. I look forward to hearing your assessment.

We are seeking an experienced Microsoft Word template specialist to examine, correct, and enhance a collection of Word templates intended for the latest Microsoft Word versions on Windows PC.

This is not purely a visual assignment. The templates also need to be technically reliable under actual user behavior, particularly when users copy and paste content from older legacy templates into the new ones.

**The assistance we would appreciate.**

1\. Carefully review this brief
2\. Examine the newest template documents along with the supporting files
3\. Respond with:
• a fixed price for the project
• a suggested timeline
• any preliminary risks or observations

⸻

Scope of Work

1\. Test the existing templates

Conduct user and functional testing of the current templates to verify that they are constructed properly and work dependably during ordinary daily use.

Testing includes:
• styles
• list behavior
• indentation logic
• tab behavior
• line breaks
• tables
• columns
• copy-paste behavior
• overall formatting stability

⸻

2\. Apply new styles to every template

Introduce the new style system specified in this document:

new\_styles\_for\_implementation\_pbu

The system must be implemented consistently in all templates.

⸻

3\. Recommend improvements

Assess the templates and propose:
• need-to-have improvements
• nice-to-have improvements

Recommendations may cover missing functionality, structural changes, usability enhancements, or technical corrections that would improve stability and make the templates easier to use.

⸻

Environment

Every template will be used with the latest Microsoft Word versions on PC.

Optimization should focus on:
• modern Word for Windows
• actual user editing behavior
• reliable use by multiple users

⸻

Customer Design Feedback to Implement

A. Indentation logic and Tab functionality

For every applicable list style, users need to be able to create sub-levels naturally with the Tab key.

Requirements:
• every list style must allow intuitive indentation into sub-levels
• the hierarchy must stay orderly and clearly structured
• list levels must use the vertical alignment logic illustrated in the brief
• nested levels must maintain consistent alignment across the document

(Refer to New\_styles\_for\_implementation\_pbu for design guides)

B. Graphic bullet design

Revise the bullet formatting so that:
• bullet dimensions are proportional to the text size
• the bullets appear visually balanced
• bullets are vertically centered against the text
• bullet scaling follows the font size naturally

C. Rename every style

If applicable to resolving copy-paste issues, all template styles must be renamed using this prefix:

PBU -

Examples:
• PBU - Heading 1
• PBU - Body Text
• PBU - Bullet List

This requirement covers all applicable styles, including:
• headings
• body text
• quotes
• list styles
• table-related styles
• any other active styles used by the templates

⸻

Customer Error Feedback to Resolve

1\. Compatibility and copy-paste stability

Users currently encounter significant formatting problems when transferring content from the older templates to the new templates.

The following old templates have been supplied for testing:
• Old\_v1.docx
• Old\_v2.docx

This workflow needs to be tested and made as stable as possible.

2\. Line break issues

Correct the problem that prevents users from reliably inserting manual line breaks after pasted content.

3\. Table and column integrity

Resolve the problems where:
• the column on the right shifts beyond the page margins when content is pasted
• table layouts become damaged during pasting

Table structures must stay fixed and dependable inside the page layout.

4\. Style break prevention

Determine whether template styles can be prevented, or at least made less likely, to break when content is pasted from legacy documents.

We recognize that Word has limitations, but the configuration should be as robust as technically possible.

⸻

Testing Requirements

Please test all of the following thoroughly:
• every list level
• bullet lists
• numbered lists
• multilevel list behavior
• tab and indentation behavior
• table behavior
• column behavior
• copying and pasting from legacy templates
• manual line breaks following pasted content
• overall layout stability

Specific test requirement

In particular, test copying and pasting from old PBU templates into V14 and confirm that:
• the layout stays stable
• style behavior is predictable
• end users can use the Tab functionality intuitively
• the list hierarchy stays aligned and usable

⸻

Deliverables

Your proposal should provide:
1\. A fixed project price
2\. An estimated timeline
3\. notes covering the recommended need-to-have and nice-to-have improvements

Upon delivery, we expect:
• revised template files
• consistent PBU naming for styles (maybe)
• the new styles implemented (Refer to New\_styles\_for\_implementation\_pbu for design guides)
• better list behavior
• greater pasting stability wherever technically possible

value_updates.right_column_overflow_constraint: The right-hand column must remain within the page margins when content is pasted.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Salma [FREELANCER_NAME_001]

Below is the initial feedback from our customer. Please tell me what you think.

Proposal \(Indstilling\):
• Placeholder fields: Unlike the Executive Summary, clicking the "insert" fields \(Advantages, settings, attachments, headline, and date\) does not automatically remove the existing text.
• Text boxes: When the text boxes on the left side, including the headline, run out of room, they do not wrap the words automatically. Instead, the right-hand column is pushed farther to the right.
• Line breaks: As a result, users must add line breaks manually. Unfortunately, using a "normal" line break \(hard return\) creates too much line spacing. That spacing works well between bullet points, but it is excessive for continuous text. A "soft return" \(Shift\+Enter\) works, although I doubt our colleagues know how to use it.
• Date function: Could the date functionality used in the "Board Seminar" document also be implemented here?
Guidance \(Vejledning\):
• Margins: The margins beneath the "\(short description\)" section are not fixed. Without manual line breaks, the "pencil" icon is progressively cut off. Can fixed margins be configured?
• Theme description: This has the same problem described in point 3 under "Proposal."
• Reflections: The section under "\(write own reflections, if any\)," has the same problem as point 1 under "Proposal."
Board Seminar \(Bestyrelsesseminar\):
• Multi-line support: Users must be able to enter multiple lines beneath "Item and Title." Manual line breaks need to work in this area.
• Agenda: The section under "\(insert agenda\)," has the same problem as point 1 under "Proposal."
Board Meeting \(Bestyrelsesmøde\):
• Date function: Can this document use the same date functionality found in the "Board Seminar" document?
• Alignment: "Item and Title" does not line up with "Topic," "Proposal," and "Start time."
• Formatting issues: Adding another line directly after a "Topic" also creates an additional horizontal line/border. Adding a line in other places behaves correctly.
Master:
• Review: [CLIENT_NAME_001] and I need to review this because the bullet sizes and spacing still look wrong on my screen.
• Tables: I need a walkthrough or explanation showing how the tables function.
• Color palette: All these colors should not be available as choices.

value_updates.left_text_box_overflow_behavior: When left-side text boxes run out of room, words must wrap automatically instead of pushing the right-hand column farther right.

routing_warnings.description: The applied row-and-column spacing addresses structured content spacing rather than containment of an overflowing column.
The Board Meeting alignment observation concerns alignment among named fields rather than column overflow containment.
The client clarifies the Board Meeting field-alignment defect, which belongs to the dedicated alignment Requirement.
